patients.summary: Former construction site supervisor with intermediate-risk AML diagnosed 2023, in remission on maintenance azacitidine/venetoclax at an outside cancer center, with hypertension and chemotherapy-induced neuropathy; joins the practice in 2024. Febrile neutropenia admission in December 2025, ICU stay for severe sepsis in February 2026, and in July 2026 an ICU admission for severe hyponatremia complicated by central pontine myelinolysis with a locked-in state.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is looking to move his primary care here. His old PCP office is cutting hours and he wants a doctor he can reach by text while he's going through cancer treatment. Gets his leukemia care at a cancer center, wants a local doc for everything else. Medicare. Explained membership and that insurance still covers labs and specialists. Booked new patient appt 9/4 at 9:00. He signed a records release over the phone portal; release faxed to his prior PCP office today. Asked him to bring all med bottles.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

54M transferring primary care. Main reason: wants one doctor he can reach between oncology visits, since the cancer center is an hour each way.

Oncologic hx (per pt, cancer center records requested): AML, told intermediate-risk cytogenetics, diagnosed March 2023 after a marrow biopsy. Port placed R chest wall at diagnosis. Inpatient induction then consolidation that year, in remission since. Since early 2024 on maintenance cycles: shots at the infusion center for a week each month plus venetoclax pills for two weeks. Several marrow biopsies so far, all OK per him. Prophylactic acyclovir and posaconazole the whole time. Oxycodone from oncology for bone aches, uses it maybe a few times a month.

Neuropathy: numb, pins-and-needles feeling in both feet since the consolidation chemo in 2023. Not painful enough to want a med. Has learned to look at his feet going down stairs. No falls.

HTN since about 2016, amlodipine 5 for years. No home cuff.

PSH: port 2023, marrow biopsies, tonsillectomy as a kid.
Allergies: Bactrim, anaphylaxis. IV contrast, hives.
Meds: reconciled from bottles, see list. Venetoclax 70 mg (7 x 10 mg) days 1-14 is the reduced dose oncology uses with the posaconazole.
FH: father lung ca, died 68. Mother DM2, HTN. Paternal uncle died at 55 of an acute leukemia, type unknown.
SH: construction site supervisor, out on disability since the diagnosis. Lives alone, single. Former smoker, ~20 pk-yr, quit 2019. Beer once or twice a week. No drugs.

ROS: energy okay between cycles, tired the week of injections. No fevers. Bowels slow on oxycodone days, uses Miralax-type powder. Otherwise negative.

EXAM
Vitals as charted. Well appearing, pleasant.
HEENT: oropharynx clear, no mucosal lesions. Neck supple, no nodes.
Chest: port R upper chest, skin intact, no erythema or tenderness.
CV: RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally.
Abd: soft, nontender, no hepatosplenomegaly palpable.
Skin: no petechiae or bruising.
Neuro: alert, fluent. Strength 5/5 throughout. Vibration and pinprick reduced in both feet up to the ankles; proprioception at the toes intact. Gait steady.
Ext: no edema.

A/P
1. AML in remission on maintenance - managed by the cancer center. Records request sent. They run his counts; I'll copy them on my labs.
2. HTN - at goal on amlodipine 5. Continue, I'll take over refills.
3. Chemo neuropathy, feet - stable, declines medication. Foot care and fall precautions talked through.
4. Health maintenance: CMP, lipids, A1c, one-time hep C and HIV today. Colonoscopy 2020 normal per prior records. Tdap 2019. Talked about vaccines for someone on chemo - flu, COVID and Prevnar 20 at a nurse visit next month, Shingrix after that. Qualifies by age and smoking history for a lung screening CT; we agreed to hold off while he's on active leukemia treatment and revisit. PHQ-9 3.
5. Bowel regimen ok.

RTC 3 months, sooner prn. He has my cell for texting.

documents.title: Hematology-oncology treatment summary (received)
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CANCER CENTER - LEUKEMIA PROGRAM
Treatment summary prepared at the request of the patient's new primary care physician.

Diagnosis: acute myeloid leukemia, intermediate-risk cytogenetics. Diagnosed March 2023 on bone marrow aspirate and biopsy. Right chest wall implanted port placed March 2023.

Treatment:
- Induction with cytarabine-based intensive chemotherapy, spring 2023. Day-28 marrow: morphologic remission.
- Consolidation with cytarabine-based cycles, summer-fall 2023. Peripheral neuropathy of the feet developed during consolidation and has persisted.
- Maintenance since early 2024: azacitidine 75 mg/m2 subcutaneously days 1-7 with venetoclax days 1-14 of each 28-day cycle. Venetoclax 70 mg daily, reduced for concomitant posaconazole.

Most recent marrow (spring 2024): continued morphologic remission.

Supportive medications: acyclovir 800 mg twice daily; posaconazole delayed-release 300 mg daily; oxycodone 5 mg every 6 hours as needed for bone pain; polyethylene glycol as needed.

Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis); iodinated contrast (hives).

Other: hypertension on amlodipine. Former smoker.

Plan: maintenance cycles monthly with counts before each cycle; marrow surveillance periodically. Please call the leukemia nurse line for fever of 100.4 or higher.

Attending hematologist-oncologist, leukemia program

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Here for vaccines ordered at his new patient visit. Timed between maintenance cycles; last injection week ended 9/30 and oncology ok'd today. Afebrile, feels well. Allergies reviewed, none to vaccine components.
Given: inactivated flu L deltoid; Pfizer COVID 2024-25 formula R deltoid; Prevnar 20 L deltoid, separate site 1 inch below flu.
Tolerated, no reaction in 15 min wait. VIS sheets given. Shingrix series to start at his December visit.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 3-month check. Doing alright. Had his December cycle last week, fatigue for a few days then back to normal. Oncology says counts fine, plan unchanged. Taking amlodipine daily. Feet the same, no falls.

O: BP and pulse as charted, weight steady. Alert, comfortable. Mouth clear. Heart regular, lungs clear. No ankle swelling. Port site fine.

A/P:
- HTN: controlled, no change. Refill sent for 90 days.
- AML on maintenance: per cancer center.
- Neuropathy: stable.
- Shingrix #1 today (recombinant, fine with his treatment). Dose 2 in 2 months, nurse visit.

Recheck spring for a wellness visit.
